Hi — related to this PR: the \`write\` tool has the same class of problem, but with a slightly different root cause.

The \`write\` tool schema defines \`content\` before \`filePath\`:

\`\`\`ts
o.Struct({
  content:  o.String.annotate(...),   // first
  filePath: o.String.annotate(...),   // second
})
\`\`\`

When local models write large files, they exhaust their token budget generating \`content\` before they ever reach \`filePath\`, producing a valid JSON object with content but no path — resulting in \`SchemaError(Missing key at ["filePath"])\`.

The fix here would be different from making the field optional (since \`filePath\` is genuinely required): simply swap the field order so \`filePath\` is declared before \`content\`. That way the model generates the path first and only the content can be truncated.

**Update:** this turns out to be a subset of #18108 which covers the full truncation/recovery failure chain in detail — worth a look if you want to address the root cause rather than just the field ordering.
Same issue in 1.15.6. So the bug exists at least from 1.14.50 till latest.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #18108: Covers the same root symptom — write tool JSON truncated when token budget is exhausted, with detailed analysis of the truncation/recovery pipeline
- #5890: Reports the same "incomplete JSON when writing files" failure mode

If your issue is specifically about the *field ordering* fix as a mitigation (putting `filePath` before `content` so the path is always captured before truncation), it may be a worthwhile complement to #18108's broader recovery-focused approach — worth clarifying the distinction in a comment there.

Marking as duplicate of #18108 which covers this and the full failure chain in much more detail. The field-order swap (filePath before content) is a useful mitigation but #18108's P0 fix (detecting truncation in repairToolCall) is the proper fix.

This proposal is related to #19919, but intentionally narrower.
Instead of adding general frontend UI extensibility, plugin-provided components, or iframe/webview rendering, this would only add a config-driven external settings link in the Settings dialog.
OpenCode would render a sidebar entry and open a configured http/https URL. The external service would own its UI, auth, API, and persistence. This avoids arbitrary frontend code injection and keeps the first PR small.
If maintainers agree this is a useful first step, I can open a focused PR for the link-only version and reference #19919 rather than trying to solve the broader plugin UI extensibility request.

Investigated this with the goal of putting up a fix. Diagnosis below — but I see you're assigned, so I'd rather check before opening a PR.

**Where the hang actually lives:** `packages/app/src/pages/session/message-timeline.data.ts` → `constructMessageRows` (~L112-250), with most of the time spent in `groupParts` from `packages/ui/src/components/message-part.tsx` (~L556) doing `parts.slice(start, end+1).map(...)` per non-context run — O(n²) over parts. Each surviving part wraps in `Data.TaggedClass` with structural-equality bookkeeping. At ~200k parts the first synchronous run never returns inside the renderer's event budget.

**Why #26949 (virtualize timeline rows) didn't fix it:** virtualization wraps row *rendering*, but the hang happens earlier in row *data construction*, before the virtualizer ever sees them.

**Why it's catastrophic:** pagination in `directory-sync.ts` is per-*message*, not per-*part*, so a single assistant message containing 100k tool parts loads in one shot.

**Smallest possible mitigation (~70 lines, one file):** in `MessageTimeline`, sum `getMsgParts(m.id).length` across the session and short-circuit `messageRowMemos` to a `TimelineRow.Truncated` row above some threshold (e.g. 20k parts). Render that as a card with "Archive" + "Render anyway" buttons. Self-heals every existing user with a poisoned DB on next launch.

**Question:** is this on your roadmap as part of the cursor-based part pagination hinted at by the TODO at `session.tsx:122`? If you've already got something in flight I'll stay out of it. If not, happy to put up the circuit-breaker as a stop-gap while the structural fix gets done. Same fix would close #28984.
